release_date_source: General availability of Windows 2000 (2000-02-17; the build 2195 RTM was released to manufacturing in December 1999), taken from the author's knowledge, not from a page re-read for this record; the dates inside the DLLs (1999-12-07) and the time stamp of the kernel32.dll export directory (1999-12-01) agree with an RTM build. age_years = days from 2000-02-17 to the trial date 2026-11-12 divided by 365.25, rounded to 0.1.
eol_source: validation/sources.json eol-windows-10: the backend (loomora_is_eol) treats every Windows with NT major version 10 or lower as end of life, so 5.0 is end of life, and the Legacy UI really showed the end-of-life banner and wrote eol_warning_shown true in every run. Microsoft ended support for Windows 2000 in July 2010 (author's knowledge, not re-read).
floor_note: Legacy floor CANDIDATE for the Windows family, only for what was actually tested on this VM (FR-005: the oldest platform on which the greeting really displays): the Legacy UI x86 executable displays 'Bonjour Coucou', updates to 'Bonjour Marie' when typed and exits cleanly on Windows 2000 build 2195 RTM in this VirtualBox VM. The decided floor of research R6 is Windows 2000 SP4, which is NOT this system (no service pack installed): is_floor stays false until the lead decides. Nothing older than this system was tried (no NT 4.0, no Windows 9x, which the UI cannot run on by design).
